name: PSRO / Double-Oracle population baseline (System 3)
authority: PI, 2026-09-06, citing VGC-Bench (Angliss et al.) and the NeurIPS 2023 StarCraft II league-training work: 'your three main systems should be Mixed PPO (no latent), Latent-conditioned policy (our method), PSRO / Double-Oracle policy population, and keep the separate specialists as an oracle/reference ceiling, not as the third baseline.'

timing_disclosure.when: written before any PSRO code exists and before any PSRO seed is spent.
visible_when_written: the complete 2v2 confirmatory chain (pi_G, pi_A/pi_B, Rung 1 latent policy)
the existing FP infrastructure and its smoke record (FP_SMOKE_RESULT.json, FP_SMOKE_PASS 9/9)
the ladder and robustness results to date
NOT_visible_when_written: any PSRO population, payoff matrix, meta-strategy, or evaluation result

WHY_THIS_REPLACES_THE_SPECIALISTS_AS_SYS.problem_shared_by_both_approaches: what do we do when one strategic behavior is not sufficient across diverse opponents?
WHY_THIS_REPLACES_THE_SPECIALISTS_AS_SYS.PSRO_answer: keep MULTIPLE independent policies plus a meta-strategy over them: {pi_1..pi_k} + Nash distribution
WHY_THIS_REPLACES_THE_SPECIALISTS_AS_SYS.our_answer: encode multiple strategic modes INSIDE one policy: pi_theta(a|s,z)
WHY_THIS_REPLACES_THE_SPECIALISTS_AS_SYS.why_the_comparison_is_sharp: both solve the same problem with opposite capacity strategies. Beating an ordinary mixed-PPO generalist only shows conditioning helps; matching a population-based method while sharing ~98% of parameters is a performance-versus-compression result, which is a stronger claim.
WHY_THIS_REPLACES_THE_SPECIALISTS_AS_SYS.specialists_are_reclassified: pi_A / pi_B become an ORACLE / REFERENCE CEILING (how much specialization exists when parameter sharing is removed entirely), NOT a competing algorithm. Existing specialist records are unchanged; only their label in the comparison table changes.

THE_FOUR_SYSTEMS.1_mixed_ppo_generalist: pi_G(a|s), trained 50/50 against Pole A and Pole B. The ablation: if latent beats this, conditioning matters.
THE_FOUR_SYSTEMS.2_latent_conditioned_OURS: pi_theta(a|s,z), z0->A, z1->B. Judged by the same crossover gate used throughout: delta_A > 0 and delta_B > 0, both LCB95 > 0.
THE_FOUR_SYSTEMS.3_psro_double_oracle: a population {pi_1..pi_k} with an empirical payoff matrix and a Nash meta-strategy over it. The literature-strength baseline.
THE_FOUR_SYSTEMS.reference_ceiling: pi_A, pi_B separate specialists -- reported as an oracle bound, not a competing system.

loop: 2. evaluate the empirical payoff matrix over all population pairs
3. solve for a meta-strategy (Nash) over the population
4. train a best response against the meta-strategy-weighted mixture
5. add the response to the population
6. repeat for a FROZEN number of iterations
ALGORITHM_FROZEN_BEFORE_IMPLEMENTATION.why_4: bounded before any result is seen, chosen for compute feasibility against the 2026-09-15 deadline rather than tuned. The stopping point is frozen here so the population cannot be grown until it happens to win.
ALGORITHM_FROZEN_BEFORE_IMPLEMENTATION.meta_strategy_solver: Nash equilibrium of the empirical zero-sum payoff matrix, computed by linear programming; if the LP is degenerate or unavailable, uniform is used and that substitution is RECORDED in the result, never silently applied.
ALGORITHM_FROZEN_BEFORE_IMPLEMENTATION.best_response_training: the same PPO recipe used everywhere else (run_g0_v5_long::build_config family), unchanged. 1,000,000 steps per best response, matching the specialist budget.
ALGORITHM_FROZEN_BEFORE_IMPLEMENTATION.payoff_matrix: win rate of row policy against column policy, evaluated on a frozen seed block, symmetric-zero-sum by construction (payoff[j][i] = 1 - payoff[i][j] is NOT assumed; both directions are measured).

WHAT_ALREADY_EXISTS_VERIFIED_NOT_ASSUMED.snapshot_POOL_training: cfg.snapshot_opponent_pool = (paths...) trains against a sampled population. SMOKE-VERIFIED 9/9 in FP_SMOKE_RESULT.json (FP_SMOKE_PASS): preload, subset, coverage, episode-hold, boundaries, determinism, no-silent-None, provenance, and learning+roundtrip, at 24k steps against a 2-checkpoint pool. This is the single most important reusable piece and it is already proven.
WHAT_ALREADY_EXISTS_VERIFIED_NOT_ASSUMED.separate_rng_stream: snapshot picks use pool.snapshot_rng (seed+902), deliberately NOT the scripted-opponent rng, so enabling a population cannot shift the scripted opponent sequence for a given seed.
WHAT_ALREADY_EXISTS_VERIFIED_NOT_ASSUMED.fail_closed_loadability_guard: gpu_env/state/snapshots.py swallows load errors and returns None, which would leave red UNPILOTED while training looked healthy -- a counterfeit success. Both _sample_snapshot_opponents and run_fictitious_play.py::assert_loadable raise instead. Any PSRO code MUST preserve this guard; a silently unpiloted opponent would corrupt every payoff-matrix entry.

WHAT_MUST_BE_BUILT.1_weighted_snapshot_sampling: snapshot sampling is currently UNIFORM: rng.integers(0, len(snapshots)) in rl/custom_ppo/curriculum_runtime.py::_sample_snapshot_opponents. PSRO requires sampling proportional to the Nash meta-strategy. Adds an optional weights field; absent weights must reproduce today's uniform behaviour EXACTLY, so fictitious play and the passing FP smoke are unaffected.
WHAT_MUST_BE_BUILT.2_empirical_payoff_matrix: evaluate every ordered population pair on a frozen seed block. Does not exist.
WHAT_MUST_BE_BUILT.3_nash_meta_strategy_solver: LP over the empirical matrix. Does not exist.
WHAT_MUST_BE_BUILT.4_psro_iteration_loop: orchestrates 1-3 plus best-response training and population growth, with per-iteration provenance. Does not exist.
WHAT_MUST_BE_BUILT.note_on_run_fictitious_play_py: its trailing note says 'SNAPSHOT-pool training wiring is the remaining step'. That note is STALE with respect to run_fp_smoke.py, which drove pool training end-to-end via cfg.snapshot_opponent_pool and passed 9/9. The mechanism exists; run_fictitious_play.py simply never wired itself to it.

SEEDS.allocation_rule: best response for iteration k uses base + k. Payoff and final evaluation blocks are disjoint from each other and from every prior allocation.
SEEDS.disjointness_verified: exact-literal grep of 15000001 / 15200001 / 15400001 against every JSON under artifacts/strategic_demand/, artifacts/strategic_demand/sppo/ and artifacts/vgc_fp/: ZERO hits. Verified immediately before this record was committed.
SEEDS.larger_team_sizes: NOT allocated here. 4v4 and 6v6 PSRO seeds are allocated only if and when those sizes are actually scheduled, to avoid reserving blocks that may never be spent.

EVALUATION.final_comparison: all systems evaluated on the SAME frozen block (15400001..15400064) against both poles, so the three-way comparison is paired rather than three independent averages.
EVALUATION.population_deployment_rule: the PSRO population is deployed under its Nash meta-strategy -- the mixture IS the system. Reporting the population's best single member against each pole would be selecting on the test set and is explicitly forbidden.
reported_quantities: per-pole win rate for each system
the parameter count of each system (the compression axis: one shared network vs k independent policies)
the crossover statistic for the latent system, unchanged
EVALUATION.bootstrap: paired percentile bootstrap over seeds, n_boot=20000, alpha=0.05, rng_seed=7 -- unchanged from every other evaluation in this program.

HONESTY_CONSTRAINTS.no_designing_psro_to_lose: PSRO is configured to the faithful algorithm, not to a weakened variant. If a design choice materially advantages the latent method, it is recorded and justified in this spec BEFORE results exist, or it is not made.
HONESTY_CONSTRAINTS.outcome_neutrality: all outcomes are publishable and pre-committed: latent beats both; latent beats the generalist but trails PSRO while using one compact network (a performance-versus-compression result); latent matches PSRO at ~98% parameter sharing (the cleanest story). None of these is treated as a failure.
HONESTY_CONSTRAINTS.compute_asymmetry_must_be_reported: PSRO trains k policies; the latent method trains one. Wall-clock and parameter count are reported alongside win rates so the comparison is not silently unfair in either direction.

SCOPE_AND_SEQUENCING.first_target: 2v2 ONLY. It is the only team size where the other three systems already exist (pi_G, pi_A/pi_B, the Rung 1 latent policy), so one PSRO run completes the full four-system comparison there.
SCOPE_AND_SEQUENCING.4v4_and_6v6: CONDITIONAL on remaining time. Neither currently has pi_G or a latent policy, so PSRO alone would not complete their comparison tables.
SCOPE_AND_SEQUENCING.known_open_gap: train_specialist_scale.py supports --policy A|B only; pi_G (the generalist, System 1) is NOT wired for 4v4/6v6. Any scaled three-system comparison needs that gap closed first.

NOT_AUTHORIZED_BY_THIS_SPEC: changing the crossover gate, the bootstrap, or any existing frozen record
modifying uniform snapshot sampling behaviour when weights are absent
growing the population beyond the frozen 4 iterations
SEQUENCE: freeze this spec -> add weighted snapshot sampling (uniform-preserving) -> build payoff matrix + Nash solver -> smoke the loop on tiny budgets with non-scientific seeds -> run 2v2 PSRO -> evaluate all four systems on the shared frozen block -> report with parameter counts and compute cost alongside win rates
